source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: In the demo's second attempt, pasting the rubric helped, but grading a second student's submission in the same chat conversation introduced a new problem. What was it?

options.text: The rubric had to be pasted in again before every new submission
options.feedback: That is not the problem identified -- the rubric stayed in context. The issue was what else stayed in context alongside it, namely the first grading.

options.text: The chat session ran out of room to hold the rubric and submissions
options.feedback: Running out of space is not the failure described. The problem was the content that carried forward, not capacity.

options.text: The model forgot the rubric once it had finished the first submission
options.feedback: The rubric was still available. What also stayed available was the first submission's grade and comments, and that is what shifted the second result.

options.text: The first grading stayed in context, so the second was judged partly against it
options.feedback: Everything earlier in a chat can influence what comes next, so a submission graded right after another is no longer judged purely on its own merits -- it can come out harsher or more lenient because of what preceded it.
